# git: pull from remote

Let `pull` target a specific remote and branch. **Motivation:** "there is no way to specify a remote for pulling." The wrapper of the time:

```bash
git-pull () {
        if ! git diff-index --quiet HEAD
        then
                git stash
                trap '{ git stash pop; }' EXIT
        fi
        git fetch --all --prune --prune-tags --tags
        git pull --force --rebase
        git submodule update --init --recursive
}
```

always pulled the tracked branch. With forks the author wants to sync a branch from the parent:

```bash
$ pull
# fetch from attached remote
$ git remote add upstream fork.git
$ pull upstream main
# fetch from specified remote
```
